summary: Nullabor Motel Airport (NUR/YNUB) is a small remote airstrip located on the vast Nullarbor Plain in southern Australia, near the border between South Australia and Western Australia. It primarily serves the adjacent Nullarbor Motel, a well-known roadhouse stop along the iconic Eyre Highway for travelers crossing one of the world's largest and most arid limestone karst landscapes. The airport provides essential access for the region's sparse population, roadhouse operations, and occasional fly-in visitors exploring the remote outback.
faqs:
Q: Where is Nullabor Motel Airport located?
A: It is situated on the Nullarbor Plain in far western South Australia, near the Western Australia border, adjacent to the Nullarbor Motel roadhouse along the Eyre Highway.

Q: Does Nullabor Motel Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, this is a small private airstrip that primarily serves general aviation, charter flights, and fly-in visitors to the motel and surrounding outback region.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a remote outback airstrip, facilities are minimal. Visitors typically rely on the adjacent Nullarbor Motel roadhouse for accommodation, meals, and fuel services.

Q: Is the airport suitable for all aircraft types?
A: The strip is best suited for small to medium general aviation aircraft. Pilots should check current conditions and any NOTAMs before flying to this remote location.
transport_tips: The airport is most commonly accessed by private or chartered aircraft, as it has no scheduled commercial service. Travelers reaching the area by road typically drive along the Eyre Highway, the main east-west route crossing the Nullarbor Plain. The closest sealed road access is directly via the Eyre Highway, and fuel stops are limited, so planning is essential.
local_tip: Time your visit around sunrise or sunset to experience the famous Nullarbor light, when the flat, treeless landscape transforms into a stunning palette of reds, oranges, and purples—ideal for photography from the motel veranda.
